L2·N12761unmasked layer
This neuron's clearest, strongest response is a large *negative* activation on sentence-terminal punctuation immediately followed by a paragraph break (".\n", "?\n"), while its mild positive firings are scattered on word-completing subword pieces/nouns in mid-sentence (e.g. "ino" in "Vino", "istry" in "Dentistry", " internet", " consideration") — i.e. it mostly marks "mid-sentence continuation vs. end-of-line boundary."

L3·N12312unmasked layer
Fires at sentence/clause-boundary punctuation — full stops, exclamation marks (often followed by a newline), and the comma after a datelined place name — i.e., the token that closes one sentence just before a new one starts (note: similar punctuation tokens also give the strongest negative values, so it's a punctuation-position feature rather than a semantic one).

This appears to be a syntactic-continuation neuron on grammatical function words mid-clause: it fires positively on modals/determiners/adverbials that open a new predicate (e.g. "that **might** occur", "that **can** stock", "used as **a** suffix", the comma before a participial "…award**,** allowing"), and is strongly suppressed on prepositions/conjunctions that merely complete a fixed collocation ("receipt **of** order", "as soon **as** possible", "workshop **and** begin", "formation **when** they").
